shots.caption: AI-generated clip
shots.text: Bombay, *1991.*

shots.caption: AI-generated clip
shots.text: India has enough foreign currency to pay for *just a few weeks* of imports.

shots.caption: AI illustration
shots.text: So it does the *unthinkable.*

shots.caption: AI illustration
shots.text: It sends the nation's *gold* abroad, as security for a loan.
Its gold is about to leave the country, in *secret.*

shots.caption: Representative image
shots.text: *August 1990.* Iraq invades Kuwait.
Oil prices *double.*
Indian workers are evacuated from the Gulf. The money they sent home *dries up.*

shots.caption: Parliament House, New Delhi
shots.text: At home, politics is in turmoil. The V. P. Singh government *falls* in November 1990.

shots.caption: Chandra Shekhar
shots.text: Chandra Shekhar becomes Prime Minister, at the head of a *minority government.*

shots.caption: Representative footage
shots.text: Ratings agencies downgrade India. Non-resident Indians *pull out* their deposits.
War abroad. Chaos at home. A *perfect storm.*

shots.caption: Budget speech, 24 July 1991
shots.text: The Finance Minister will later tell Parliament: “We have been *at the edge of a precipice* since December 1990.”

shots.caption: AI-generated clip
shots.text: Reserves keep falling, month after month.
Imports left: *2 weeks.*

shots.caption: AI-generated clip
shots.text: India is close to *defaulting* on its foreign debt, for the first time ever.

shots.caption: Reserve Bank of India, Mumbai
shots.text: The country has one big asset left: *gold.*

shots.caption: AI illustration
shots.text: The first gold to go is government gold, *seized from smugglers.*

shots.label: MAY 1991  ·  VIA SBI TO UNION BANK OF SWITZERLAND

shots.text: Sold, with an option to *buy it back.*

shots.caption: Rajiv Gandhi
shots.text: *21 May 1991.* In the middle of an election campaign, Rajiv Gandhi is assassinated.

shots.caption: P. V. Narasimha Rao
shots.text: In June, P. V. Narasimha Rao becomes Prime Minister.

shots.caption: Manmohan Singh (later photo)
shots.text: His surprise choice for Finance Minister: the economist *Manmohan Singh.*

shots.caption: AI illustration
shots.text: In three days, the rupee loses *nearly a fifth* of its value.
Destination: *London.*

shots.caption: Representative footage (modern aircraft)
shots.text: Under tight security, the gold is flown out on a *chartered cargo plane.*
Over two weeks in July, *46.91 tonnes* of gold are flown from Bombay to London.

shots.caption: AI-generated clip · London
shots.text: The gold goes into the vaults of the *Bank of England.*

shots.caption: Bank of England, London
shots.text: It is pledged to the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan...

shots.caption: Bank of Japan, Tokyo
shots.text: ...for a loan of about *$400 million.*
Loan: *$400 million.*
Two central banks. One loan. *India's gold* as security.

shots.caption: AI illustration
shots.text: When the news breaks, the country is *stunned.*

shots.title: An Idea Whose Time Has Come

shots.caption: Parliament House, New Delhi
shots.text: *24 July 1991.* Manmohan Singh rises in Parliament to present his first Budget.
A Finance Minister quotes *Victor Hugo.*
“No power on earth can stop *an idea whose time has come.*”
shots.caption: Victor Hugo, quoted in the Budget speech
AI illustration
shots.text: Licences, quotas and controls begin to fall. India *opens up* to the world.

shots.caption: RBI Monetary Museum, Mumbai
shots.text: By the end of 1991, the loans are repaid. The pledge is *released.*

shots.caption: Today
shots.text: Today, India holds one of the *largest foreign exchange reserves* in the world.
Gold home: *100 tonnes.*
In 2024, the RBI brings about *100 tonnes* of its gold home from the UK.
India didn't just survive 1991. *It was reborn.*
